gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the deciding check on one APDO line: ChargerLAB's POWER-Z readout of Samsung's own 60 W adapter (EP-T6010) shows three PPS ranges (5–11 V 5 A, 5–16 V 4 A, 5–21 V 3 A) over plain PD 3.0, and Android Authority says the S26 Ultra needs the 20 V/3 A one from a single port. So the check is a PPS range that reaches 20–21 V at 3 A on one port. The 'PD 3.1' badge from Samsung's footnote is not it, and neither are a fixed 20 V/3 A PDO, a high-current PPS range that stops at 11 V or 16 V, or the 65 W headline.
standout_why: I compared this against the pages ChatGPT cited: SamMobile on the Trio (the Trio gives only 45 W, as 20 V 2.25 A PPS), Samsung CA/AE (PPS 5–20 V 3 A, plus a footnote asking for PD 3.1 and Direct Charging), the ChargerLAB EP-T6010 teardown (it lists the APDOs and 51.54 W on the S26 Ultra, but never says which range the phone draws) and itechguides. ChatGPT's answer already tells shoppers to look for 'PPS 3.3–21 V ⎓ 3 A' and warns that a fixed 20 V/3 A PDO doesn't count. Two things are new. First, ChargerLAB's tester reads Samsung's own adapter as PD 3.0, which contradicts Samsung's 'PD 3.1 or higher' footnote, so a shopper can't filter chargers on a PD 3.1 badge. Second, an 11 V or 16 V PPS range is not enough even when its rated watts look adequate. That only refines what the rival pages already say. It doesn't decide anything they leave open.
decides: It confirms the Samsung EP-T6010 as the safe pick, the only charger with a published S26 Ultra test: Android Authority measured a 60 W peak for about 2 minutes, about 48 W for about 16 minutes and 42 minutes to full; ChargerLAB measured 51.54 W. A third-party charger, ours included, can sit alongside it only if its maker states a PPS range of at least 20 V at 3 A on the port the phone uses, while that port is the only one in use. I could not reopen any UGREEN or Baseus spec table today because us.ugreen.com returned 403/429. So the UGREEN Nexode 65W travel charger, UGREEN Nexode Air 65W and Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 rest on our earlier records, are paper matches only, and none has a measured S26 Ultra result. The Samsung 65W Trio is the well-known charger that fails this check (20 V 2.25 A PPS = 45 W, per SamMobile).
